title: Noise-absorber strategy for burn alert resilience
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: After the capacity regression on 2026-03-04 we observed a series of short-lived burn spikes that produced a high volume of pageable SLO alerts. These spikes were largely transient (10-90s) and correlated with autoscaler flapping and noisy tail latencies from a model variant rollout. This ticket defines a pragmatic, multi-layered "noise-absorber" plan to reduce noisy pages while preserving meaningful escalations for genuine platform degradations. Goals: 1) cut actionable pager volume by >= 60% for transient burns; 2) eliminate duplicate pages for the same root cause; 3) maintain end-to-end SLO visibility and diagnostic fidelity. This ticket coordinates config changes, short-term automations, and a follow-up evaluation window. It includes owners, acceptance criteria, and rollback/runbook notes.
postmortem_summary: Root cause: autoscaler oscillation combined with a model variant that temporarily increased median token latency on a subset of shards. Observed effect: repeated burn-rate alerts triggered for overlapping time windows; paging thresholds lacked hysteresis and there was no short-term deduping across regional signals. Decision: implement short delay-based smoothing at the burn calculation layer, introduce a circuit-breaker dedup key by root-cause fingerprint, and tier paging so only high-confidence, repeated burns escalate to pagers immediately. Low-confidence single-window burns should create tickets or Slack notifications rather than urgent pages.
implementation_notes:
Planned changes (small, reversible): 
- Reduce burn alert sensitivity by adding a 90s sliding median smoothing before burn-rate evaluation (owner: Marco Li).
- Add a dedup fingerprint that combines impacted route, model-version, and error-family; dedup window = 5m for paging (owner: Priya Shah).
- Introduce a two-path pager: immediate pages for high-impact customers/regions or sustained (>3m) burns; otherwise route to on-call queue with low-priority flag and post to #slo-alerts channel (owner: Ops SRE).
- Create a temporary autoscaler stabilization throttle: block scale-in/on-demand scaling events for 2m after a scale decision to prevent flapping (owner: infra team).
- Dashboard and alerting playbook updates (PRs linked below).
Rollback plan: revert smoothing and dedup settings in config flags and escalate to emergency runbook if pages drop below expected sensitivity or latency regressions are missed.
acceptance_criteria: Pager volume attributable to transient burns is reduced by >= 60% during the 14-day evaluation window compared to baseline (baseline window: 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-07).
No increase in missed high-severity SLO regressions — validated by synthetic traffic that exercises the previous regression pattern.
Dedup fingerprint suppresses duplicate pages for the same root cause across regions >80% of the time.
Runbook updated and on-call team briefed; on-call responders can toggle the smoothing flag in config within 2 minutes.
Telemetry: per-route burn-rate, per-route page count, time-to-ack, and false-suppression metric are visible on the SLO console dashboard.

false_suppressions_detected - synthetic traffic should flag any suppression that hides a real regression
